info.description:
This is the REST API of Nzyme. The Nzyme web interface uses the same API, so
everything you can do in the web interface you can also do from a script, a CLI or any other client.
The interactive version of this documentation lives at https://api.docs.nzyme.org.

## Authentication

Create an API key on your user profile page in the web interface and send it as a bearer token with
every request:

```
Authorization: Bearer nzk_...
```

An API key carries the permissions of the user that created it, including the organization and tenant
scope, the organization administrator or super administrator level, feature permissions and tap
scope. Permissions are evaluated on every request, so changes to the user take effect immediately.
Keys can expire, and a key that has expired or was deleted is rejected with `401`.

Endpoints that manage credentials, such as passwords, multi-factor authentication, API keys and
sessions, require an interactive session and reject API keys. The web interface session ID is also a
bearer token, so the same requests work from a browser session.

## Permissions

Each endpoint states the permission it requires. The levels are, from lowest to highest:

* **Any user.** Every authenticated user. Data is still limited to what the user may see.
* **Organization administrator.** Manages one organization and all of its tenants.
* **Super administrator.** Manages the whole Nzyme installation.

Some endpoints additionally require a feature permission, for example `alerts_manage`. Organization
administrators and super administrators hold all feature permissions implicitly.

## Scoping

Most data endpoints take `organization_id` and `tenant_id` query parameters, because all captured data
belongs to a tenant. A request for a tenant the user cannot access returns `404`, not `403`, so that
the existence of other tenants is not revealed.

Endpoints that return captured data also take a `taps` parameter: a comma separated list of tap UUIDs,
or `*` for all taps the user can access. Users can be limited to a subset of the taps of their tenant.

## Time ranges

Endpoints that query captured data take a `time_range` query parameter. It is a URL encoded JSON
object with one of three shapes:

```
{"type": "relative", "minutes": 60}
{"type": "absolute", "from": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z"}
{"type": "named", "name": "today"}
```

Named ranges are `today`, `yesterday`, `week_to_date`, `month_to_date` and `all_time`. Timestamps are
ISO 8601. All timestamps in responses are ISO 8601 in UTC.

## Filters

List endpoints that support filtering take a `filters` query parameter. It is a URL encoded JSON
object keyed by field name. Each field maps to a list of conditions that must all be true:

```
{"ip_address": [{"field": "ip_address", "operator": "IN_CIDR", "value": "10.0.0.0/8"}]}
```

Operators are `EQUALS`, `NOT_EQUALS`, `EQUALS_NUMERIC`, `NOT_EQUALS_NUMERIC`, `REGEX_MATCH`,
`NOT_REGEX_MATCH`, `STARTS_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `CONTAINS`, `NOT_CONTAINS`, `LENGTH_EQUALS`,
`LENGTH_GREATER_THAN`, `LENGTH_SMALLER_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN`, `SMALLER_THAN`, `IN_CIDR`, `NOT_IN_CIDR`,
`IS_PRIVATE`, `IS_NOT_PRIVATE`, `IS_EMPTY`, `IS_NOT_EMPTY`, `IS_NULL` and `BOOLEAN`. The fields a given
endpoint accepts are the columns offered by the filter builder of the web interface for the same page.

## Pagination and sorting

List endpoints take `limit` and `offset` query parameters and return the total count next to the page
of results, so you can page through everything. Where sorting is supported, `order_column` names a
column of the result and `order_direction` is `ASC` or `DESC`.

## Errors

Nzyme uses HTTP status codes. `401` means the request was not authenticated or the user may not
perform the action, `404` means the resource does not exist or is outside the scope of the user,
`400` means the request could not be parsed or failed validation, and `422` means a quota is exhausted
or a configuration constraint was violated. Error responses carry no body unless the endpoint
documents one. Where a body is documented, it is a JSON object with a single `message` field that
explains the problem.

## Versioning

The spec you are reading matches a specific Nzyme release. Every node also serves the spec of its own
version at `/api/docs/openapi.json`, so a client can discover exactly what the node it talks to
supports. The API follows the Nzyme release cycle. Breaking changes are called out in the release
notes.

tags.name: Tenants

tags.name: Ping

tags.description: Detection alerts are raised by the detection engines of Nzyme. Repeated observations of the same condition update one alert instead of creating a new one, and an alert that was last seen within the past five minutes counts as active. This group of endpoints lists, resolves and deletes alerts and manages which event actions are subscribed to which detection type.

externalDocs.description: Alerting in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Alerts

tags.description: Bluetooth devices that the Bluetooth adapters of your taps discovered in range, over Bluetooth Classic, Bluetooth Low Energy or both. The data includes device names, manufacturers, device classes, discovered services and signal strength.
tags.name: Bluetooth

tags.description: Context is the knowledge you attach to an identifier, a MAC address or a network in CIDR notation, as a short name, a description and free form notes. Nzyme shows it everywhere the identifier appears in the web interface. Context always belongs to one tenant and is not shared across tenants.

externalDocs.description: Context in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Context

tags.description: A bandit is a malicious WiFi device that Nzyme alerts on when it shows up in range. Bandits are identified by the fingerprints of the frames they send. Nzyme ships built in bandits for common attack platforms like the WiFi Pineapple or the Flipper Zero, and you can define your own custom bandits per tenant.

externalDocs.description: WiFi bandits in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Bandits

tags.description: WiFi clients that taps recorded on the air. A client is connected if it was seen exchanging frames with an access point, and disconnected if it was only seen probing or sending frames that are not tied to a BSSID.
tags.name: Clients

tags.description: Nzyme calls deauthentication and disassociation frames disconnection frames, or disco frames. They are a common part of WiFi attacks that kick clients off a network. These endpoints show the disconnection activity your taps recorded and manage the disconnection monitor of a monitored network.

externalDocs.description: Disconnection activity in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Disconnection Monitoring

tags.description: Physical location of WiFi signal sources. Nzyme trilaterates a BSSID or a client from the signal strength that the taps placed on a floor plan recorded. The tap selector is not used here: Nzyme always considers all taps on the floor that the calling user can access.

externalDocs.description: WiFi trilateration in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Trilateration

tags.description: A monitored network describes the expected state of one of your own WiFi networks so that Nzyme can alert on any deviation. This group also covers SSID monitoring, probe request monitoring and the known clients of a monitored network.

externalDocs.description: Network monitoring in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Monitoring

tags.description: Access points, BSSIDs and SSIDs that taps recorded on the air. Use these endpoints to explore the WiFi networks around your taps and their signal behavior.
tags.name: Networks

tags.description: ARP requests and replies that taps recorded on the Ethernet network, with statistics and histograms of the most active requesters and responders. Nzyme also uses ARP traffic to enrich the asset inventory.
tags.name: ARP

tags.description: An asset is a device Nzyme detected in the monitored Ethernet traffic, identified by its MAC address. Nzyme builds this inventory passively and uses it to enrich MAC addresses with the hostnames and IP addresses of the asset, its DHCP fingerprints and when it was first and last seen.
tags.name: Assets

tags.description: DHCP transactions that taps recorded on the Ethernet network, including client and server addresses, offered and requested IP addresses, DHCP fingerprints and timelines. Nzyme also uses DHCP traffic to enrich the asset inventory, and its fingerprints help to detect spoofing.
tags.name: DHCP

tags.description: DNS queries and responses that taps recorded on the Ethernet network, with traffic statistics, client and server pairs and the entropy log of suspicious query names.

externalDocs.description: DNS in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: DNS

tags.description: Everything Nzyme knows about a single IP address seen on the Ethernet network, including the assets that used it, network context and geo information.
tags.name: IP Addresses

tags.description: Layer 4 traffic that taps recorded on the Ethernet network. Nzyme reassembles TCP sessions and groups UDP traffic into conversations, and reports both as sessions with traffic statistics and histograms of the busiest addresses, MAC addresses and ports.
tags.name: L4

tags.description: NAT traversal activity that taps recorded on the Ethernet network. Nzyme reports it in two views: STUN discoveries, where a device asks a public STUN server what its own public address looks like, and STUN connections, where two peers negotiate a direct or TURN relayed path to each other.
tags.name: NAT

tags.description: Portal integrity reports record what a tap received when it probed a control URL, including every redirect hop and a verdict with the reasons behind it. Use them to detect captive portals, redirects and tampered responses on a network.
tags.name: Portal Integrity

tags.description: RTSP streams that Nzyme taps observed on the network. RTSP is what cameras, network video recorders and streaming appliances use to negotiate live audio and video. Nzyme reads the clear text control connection and links the media flow back to it, so a stream reports its negotiation state, its authentication posture and the devices on both ends.
tags.name: RTSP

tags.description: SSH sessions that Nzyme taps observed on the network, including the client and server software versions exchanged during the initial unencrypted handshake. Each session is tracked over its lifetime and keyed by its underlying TCP session.

externalDocs.description: SSH in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: SSH

tags.description: SOCKS4, SOCKS4A and SOCKS5 tunnels that Nzyme taps observed on the network, including the tunnel endpoints, the authentication status and the tunneled destination. Each tunnel is tracked over its lifetime and keyed by its underlying TCP session.

externalDocs.description: SOCKS in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: SOCKS

tags.description: Time synchronization traffic that Nzyme taps observed on the network. This currently covers NTP transactions, including the exchanged timestamps and the resulting clock offset.
tags.name: Time

tags.description: WebRTC sessions that Nzyme taps observed on the network. WebRTC carries live audio and video and the data channels of browser and app based calls, screen shares and remote control tools. Nzyme recognizes a session when a STUN negotiation also carries RTP or DTLS, and reports what the connection is carrying rather than how it was established.

externalDocs.description: WebRTC in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: WebRTC

tags.description: A location groups the taps of a tenant that are deployed at the same physical site, for example a campus or a building, and can have floors with floor plans. These endpoints return the high-level status of a location: its floors, its taps, active detection alerts and environmental data. Creating and changing locations is part of the tenant settings.

externalDocs.description: Locations in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Locations

tags.description: Metrics exporters make internal Nzyme metrics available to third party monitoring systems. Exported metrics are always specific to the node you talk to.

externalDocs.description: Metrics exporters in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Metrics Exporters

tags.description: Monitors turn a saved search filter into a persistent alert condition. Nzyme runs each monitor in its configured interval and raises a MONITOR_TRIGGERED detection event when the number of results in the lookback window is larger than the trigger condition. Monitors exist for several subsystems, for example WiFi and Bluetooth.

externalDocs.description: Monitors in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Monitors

tags.description: The TLS certificates of the Nzyme web interface and API, and the PGP keys that Nzyme uses to encrypt sensitive data in the database.
tags.name: Crypto

tags.description: Shows how much data Nzyme stores per data category, and lets you purge data or change its retention time.

externalDocs.description: Retention times in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Database

tags.description: An event action is something Nzyme does when an event fires, for example sending an email, posting to a webhook or sending a syslog message. An action only runs once it is subscribed to a system event type or a detection type. Actions created in the system scope belong to no organization and can only be subscribed to system events.

externalDocs.description: Action types in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Event Actions

tags.description: System events record what happened in Nzyme itself, for example a user signing in or an organization being changed. They are either super administrator events, which affect the whole cluster, or organization events. Event actions can be subscribed to every event type.

externalDocs.description: Alerting in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Events

tags.description: Health indicators continuously check parts of an Nzyme cluster and report problems that need attention. An indicator raises a system event every time its result level changes, so you can subscribe event actions to it.
tags.name: Health

tags.description: Plugins extend Nzyme with additional functionality. These endpoints report which plugins a node loaded.
tags.name: Plugins

tags.description: The registry holds the configuration values of an Nzyme cluster.
tags.name: Registry

tags.description: System-wide settings of an Nzyme cluster: version information, subsystems and the look and feel of the web interface.
tags.name: System

tags.description: Logging in and out of Nzyme, and setting up or passing the multi-factor authentication challenge of a session. Nzyme requires multi-factor authentication for every user unless an administrator disabled it for that account.
tags.name: Authentication

tags.description: Creates the first super administrator of a fresh Nzyme installation.
tags.name: Initial Setup

tags.description: Organizations are the top level of the Nzyme tenancy model. They hold tenants, users, taps and their own configuration and quotas.
tags.name: Organizations

tags.description: A cluster consists of one or more Nzyme nodes that share a database. These endpoints expose the nodes, the message bus and the tasks queue that connect them.
tags.name: Cluster

tags.description: Nzyme Connect is an optional cloud service that your cluster reports to. In return it provides curated operational data, for example GeoIP, ASN, UAV and MAC address vendor information. All it needs is an API key.
tags.name: Nzyme Connect

tags.description: Configuration of the services Nzyme talks to, for example the SMTP server it uses to send system and alert emails. Integrations are configured for the whole cluster and not per tenant.
tags.name: Integrations

tags.description: Taps are the sensors that capture network data and report it to Nzyme.
tags.name: Taps

tags.description: A timeline shows how the parameters of a WiFi access point or network changed over time, addressed by BSSID or by SSID. A background task computes the timeline events from the changes it sees between periods, which makes timelines a tool for investigation rather than for alerting.

externalDocs.description: WiFi timelines in the Nzyme documentation

tags.name: Timelines

tags.description: Unmanned aerial vehicles that your taps detected by decoding the Remote ID broadcasts of the UAV. These endpoints return detected UAVs with their flight vectors and timelines, and manage classifications, custom UAV types and the monitoring configuration. Nzyme is not a Counter UAS platform and only sees UAVs that broadcast Remote ID.
tags.name: UAV

tags.description: Endpoints the calling user can use to manage their own profile, password, multi-factor authentication and API keys.
tags.name: User Profile

description.description: Description of the asset. Up to 32 characters.

name.description: Short name of the asset. Up to 12 characters.

notes.description: Free form notes about the asset.

filters.description: JSON encoded filter definition as produced by the web interface filter builder.

interval.description: How often the monitor runs, in minutes. Must be 1 or higher.

lookback.description: How far back the monitor looks on each run, in minutes. Must be 1 or higher.

taps.description: Tap UUIDs the monitor runs against.

items.description: Tap UUIDs the monitor runs against.

trigger_condition.description: Number of matching results that triggers the monitor. Must be 0 or higher.

UpdateMonitoredProbeRequestRequest.description: Body for updating a monitored probe request SSID of a tenant.

notes.description: Free form notes about this monitored probe request.

ssid.description: SSID to watch for in WiFi probe requests.

UpdateNetworkContextRequest.description: Body for updating network context of a tenant.

description.description: Description of the network. Up to 32 characters.

name.description: Short name of the network. Up to 12 characters.

notes.description: Free form notes about the network.

UpdatePasswordRequest.description: Body for setting the password of a user.

UpdateSidebarTitleRequest.description: Body for updating the sidebar title of the web interface.

subtitle.description: Subtitle shown below the title in the sidebar. Omit for no subtitle.

UpdateSimilarSSIDNetworkMonitorConfigura.description: Body for updating the similar SSID monitor configuration of a monitored WiFi network.

threshold.description: Similarity of an SSID in percent that triggers an alert. Between 0 and 100.

UpdateSyslogEventActionRequest.description: Body for updating a syslog event action.

description.description: New description of the event action.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the syslog receiver.

name.description: New name of the event action.

port.description: Port of the syslog receiver. Between 1 and 65535.

syslog_hostname.description: Hostname Nzyme reports as the source of the syslog messages.

UpdateTLSWildcardNodeMatcherRequest.description: Body for updating the node matcher of a TLS wildcard certificate.

node_matcher.description: Java regular expression matched against node names to decide which nodes use this certificate.

floor.description: UUID of the floor of the tenant location the tap is placed on.

latitude.description: Latitude of the tap in decimal degrees. Between -90 and 90.

location.description: UUID of the tenant location the tap is placed in.

longitude.description: Longitude of the tap in decimal degrees. Between -180 and 180.

UpdateTenantLocationRequest.description: Body for updating a location of a tenant.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location in decimal degrees. Between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location in decimal degrees. Between -180 and 180.

mfa_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes a user has to complete multi-factor authentication. Minimum is 1.

session_inactivity_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes of inactivity after which a session is closed. Minimum is 1.

session_timeout_minutes.description: Maximum lifetime of a session, in minutes. Minimum is 1.

UpdateTrackDetectorConfigurationRequest.description: Body for updating the signal track detector configuration of a WiFi network.

frame_threshold.description: Minimum number of minutes with recorded frames required to start a new track.

gap_threshold.description: Maximum number of minutes without recorded frames allowed before a track ends.

signal_centerline_jitter.description: Maximum deviation from the track centerline in dBm that still counts as part of the track.

tap_id.description: UUID of the tap this configuration applies to.

UpdateUavCustomTypeRequest.description: Body for updating a custom UAV type of a tenant.

default_classification.description: Classification applied to matching UAVs. Omit to leave them unknown.

match_type.description: How the match value is compared to the serial number of a UAV.

match_value.description: UAV serial number or serial number prefix to match.

model.description: Model of the UAV, for example "DJI Mavic 3 Pro".

name.description: Name or description of the matched UAV.

UpdateUserOwnPasswordRequest.description: Body for changing the password of the calling user.

current_password.description: Current password of the calling user.

UpdateUserPermissionsRequest.description: Body for setting the feature permissions of a user.

permissions.description: Identifiers of the feature permissions the user is granted.

items.description: Identifiers of the feature permissions the user is granted.

disable_mfa.description: Set to true to disable multi-factor authentication for this user.

email.description: Email address of the user. It is also the login name.

UpdateUserTapPermissionsRequest.description: Body for setting the tap permissions of a user.

allow_access_all_tenant_taps.description: Set to true to give the user access to all taps of the tenant.

taps.description: UUIDs of the taps the user may access. Ignored when access to all tenant taps is allowed.

items.description: UUIDs of the taps the user may access. Ignored when access to all tenant taps is allowed.

UpdateWebhookEventActionRequest.description: Body for updating a webhook event action.

allow_insecure.description: Set to true to accept invalid or untrusted TLS certificates.

bearer_token.description: Bearer token sent in the Authorization header. Omit for no authentication.

description.description: New description of the event action.

name.description: New name of the event action.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL that Nzyme posts the event to.

apiKey.description: Nzyme API key (or interactive session ID) as bearer token.
